It also shows Tier 2 ratings for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), and environmental hazards, reflecting an expanded perspective beyond formal GHS classifications. While oral hazards are considered low to moderate (Tier 3), data is deficient (Tier 4) for endocrine disruption, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards, meaning these risks are currently unknown.
